listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Tuesday, November 17. Here is what matters today. Our lead story is from the war in Ukraine. Ukraine's forces targeted a key rail and road bridge between Russia and the Crimean Peninsula for a second day. Russia says it downed more than fourteen hundred Ukrainian drones. Moscow's forces, meanwhile, fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv. Details on damage are still developing. On the front page, California is suing OpenAI over hacking risks. The state's attorney general began investigating after the Hugging Face attack. The attorney general now says that attack was entirely foreseeable because of OpenAI's security practices. Also in technology and policy, the United States has tightened controls on remote access to advanced AI chips. The new rule closes a loophole that let Chinese companies reach those chips remotely, even though physical sales to China are restricted. In sports, the 49ers beat the Cowboys forty-six to forty in Week 10. Christian McCaffrey kept setting records along the way. Now a quick look at each section. In tech and AI, the latest Claude Platform release notes are out. A protocol called AG-UI is trending on GitHub for connecting AI agents to apps. And a Hacker News post claims Windows 11 collects data on which coding agents you use. In politics, The Lever asks whether Democrats could use reconciliation to pass their agenda with fifty-one Senate votes. Drop Site News covers burning oil tankers in Hormuz and a Senate leadership battle. NPR looks at what Democratic midterm wins could mean for diversity initiatives. In world news, Ukraine says Russia targeted a rescue operation after a double-tap strike that killed seventy-two people. Japan scrambled jets after an alleged Russian incursion into its airspace. And Mozambique's opposition leader Venâncio Mondlane faces trial over the deadly 2024 election unrest. In sports, the Rockets lost to the Heat, one twenty-eight to one ten. ESPN explains Mike Evans' Achilles injury. And Amanda Nunes wants a rematch with Kayla Harrison. In Atlanta, a nineteen billion dollar regional plan includes money for The Stitch park. A Chamblee mixed-use complex is recovering after a fire. And Georgia House Republicans chose a new minority leader. In architecture, AEC Magazine looks beyond BIM toward engineering intelligence. Two new projects to see are House in Akashi and HaloPlaza in Hangzhou. In science and nature, Perseverance studied ancient Martian rocks called Idubi. Indonesia plans a marine protected area for whale sharks. And Science News looks at the focus on AI and quantum research. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Russia downs over 1,400 Ukrainian drones as Kyiv hits a key bridge in Crimea
lead.note: Ukraine's forces targeted a key rail and road bridge between Russia and the Crimean Peninsula for a second day, according to NPR. The headline reports that Russia downed more than 1,400 Ukrainian drones. At the same time, Moscow's forces fired ballistic missiles and drones at Kyiv. The summary does not give details on damage or casualties, so the full picture is still developing. The story matters because it shows both sides hitting major transport links and a capital city within the same day. The bridge is described as a key connection between Russia and Crimea, and it has now been a target on two consecutive days. Readers who want the latest on the damage and the effect on traffic should watch for follow-up reports through the day.
